submission.natural_language_explanation: A part-of-speech dial read through GELU's dip: the negative pole is near its 0.17 ceiling on open-class words in a predicate or verb slot (finite lexical verbs right after a subject, most reliably past-tense '-ed' forms like showed, turned, wanted, reported, bought; also relational or quantity nouns like number, majority, percentage, and predicate adjectives) and on mid-word fragments, while it stays near zero (pre-activation about -3) on closed-class tokens such as articles, prepositions, conjunctions, pronouns, auxiliaries (was, were, had) and punctuation. It also reads inactive on many concrete or topical nouns and attributive adjectives that come straight after 'the' or 'a' (house, milk, cat, 'a bright one'), because those push the pre-activation positive. Position 0 always sits at about 0.09.
